searchText: <@!194432762315407360> I understand that not everyone works on the weekend. 🙂 I would still really appreciate your feedback on the EIP I created, since you have experience drafting network specification EIPs for Ethereum, and you are far more familiar with the current spec than I am. > The thing that we *can* do is do things to make it easier to Merkle-prove history (eg. EIP 2935) so you can do whatever history-dependent things you want with witnesses <@!273808422753796097> Is it easier than requesting the txHash? I understand it is potentially more flexible but in practice, seems a lot cheaper (in terms of coreDev time and potentially gas) to simply have an opcode to export all aspects of the transaction, including the txHash. I just finished reading about EIP-2718, and it seems it is split between EIP-2976 (Spec for transaction type) and EIP-2972 (Legacy transaction type) does this make 2718 obsolete? 2976 depends on 2718 (it is a new transaction type). yea i missed "over Gossip" part of 2976 thanks Sorry, 2972 is the new transaction type built on 2718, 2976 is for actually gossipping 2718 transactions (necessary for them to actually work). All 3 used to be in one EIP, but they were split to help with clarity.

excerpts.author: guthl_starkware
excerpts.content:
> The thing that we *can* do is do things to make it easier to Merkle-prove history (eg. EIP 2935) so you can do whatever history-dependent things you want with witnesses
<@!273808422753796097> 

Is it easier than requesting the txHash? I understand it is potentially more flexible but in practice, seems a lot cheaper (in terms of coreDev time and potentially gas) to simply have an opcode to export all aspects of the transaction, including the txHash.
